figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Ping-pong chain elongation mechanism at the ACP·KS
interface. An acyl substrate is delivered to the KS by ACP during
chain elongation. Here, a catalytic Cys-His-His triad plays a key role
in the two-step process of transacylation and condensation. An
oxyanion hole is formed in the KS by Cys and Phe backbone amides,
highlighted with a yellow circle, which stabilizes the tetrahedral
intermediates formed during each step. The two active site histidines
participate in the decarboxylative condensation step.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Mitochondrial acyl carrier protein (mACP, orange) shuttles
intermediates through sequential enzymatic steps in the pathway.
OXSM (blue) catalyzes the first step in the elongation cycle. The
post-translational state of mACP is represented by a curved line.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Crystal structures of the OXSM obligate dimer (OXSM·
OXSM′) in the cross-linked complex with substrate mimetic-bound
mACP. For both structures, OXSM, OXSM′, and mACP are shown in
periwinkle blue, cyan, and orange, respectively. (a) Structure of
C8αBr-mACP = OXSM (PDB: 9N50). The C8αBr cross-linker is
shown in pink. (b) Structure of C8βCl-mACP = OXSM (PDB:
9N51). The C8βCl cross-linker is shown in lime (=denotes covalent
cross-linking).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Cross-linker interactivity mimics substrate positioning. (a)
Close-up of the cross-linker within the C8αBr-mACP = OXSM
complex. To enhance confidence in the precise positioning toward the
end of the acyl tail, we performed additional validation of the modeled
coordinates using polder omit maps generated in Phenix (Supporting
Figure S5).22 (b) Alignment of C8αBr (top) and C8βCl (bottom)
cross-linkers with the acyl-mACP loaded with its natural C8 substrate
(middle). Yellow and cyan lines depict the terminus of the 4′-
phosphopantetheine (PPant) arm and start of the acyl group,
respectively. (c) Close-up of the cross-linker within the C8βCl-
mACP = OXSM complex.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 5
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 5. Key interface and loop interactions between mACP and OXSM. Structure of the C8βCl-mACP = OXSM contains two sets of single
cross-linked complexes captured in one cell unit due to tNCS. OXSM, OXSM′, and mACP are shown in periwinkle blue, cyan, and orange,
respectively. Close-up view of electrostatic interactions between OXSM and (a, b) helix II of mACP, (c) helix III of mACP, and (d) hydrophobic
interactions between OXSM and mACP. Key interactions were also observed between mACP and OXSM at the loop regions. (e) Asn451, which
caps loop 1, forms hydrogen bonding with Asp310 from loop 2 to help open the gate for substate delivery and release, and (f) His313 from loop 2
interacts with Asp43 from mACP, and Thr315 forms hydrogen binding with the PPant on mACP to stabilize the substrate.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 6
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 6. OXSM has two acyl binding tunnels. (a) The substrate acyl
tail in both structures (C8βCl-mACP = OXSM shown) adopts the
top tunnel, as the bottom one is blocked by Met154. (b) Alignment of
the acyl tail positions across a subset of KS structures. The positions
of the active site Ser44 of mACP and Cys209 of the OXSM are
shown. While the acyl tail in most structures occupies the canonical
bottom tunnel, C16αBr-AcpP = FabF (orange, PDB: 6OKG) adopts
the top binding tunnel. Canonical (blue) and noncanonical or bent
(orange) tunnels are highlighted.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 7
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 7. Analysis of middle gate residue Phe447 and back gate
residue Met154. (a) Structural alignment of C8βCl-mACP = OXSM
(periwinkle blue), C8αBr-mACP = OXSM (purple), apo-OXSM
(yellow, PDB: 2IWY), and C6-acyl-OXSM (coral, PDB: 2IWZ).
Met154 did not move in these structures and remained as a block for
the canonical tunnel. On the contrary, we found that the Phe447
residue rotated depending on its substrate and mACP interactivity.
(b) Cross-linking reactions with the longer chain mACP and two
OXSM mutants Met154Gly and Met154Phe. These two mutants
acted in a similar manner, which is contradictory to the hypothesized
function of Met154 as a back gate to access longer chain fatty acids.
Full-length gels are provided within the Supporting Information.
